The euro is launched as a currency in 11 European countries.
Luna 1 launches, the first spacecraft to reach the Moon's vicinity.
Alaska becomes the 49th US state.
NASA's Spirit rover lands on Mars.
Henry Ford announces a $5 workday, doubling typical factory pay.
Samuel Morse first demonstrates his electric telegraph.
Galileo spots the moons of Jupiter through his telescope.
The United States pays off its national debt, the only time it has done so.
Jean-Pierre Blanchard makes the first balloon flight in North America.
The London Underground opens, the world's first underground railway.
Amelia Earhart flies solo from Hawaii to California.
NASA launches Deep Impact to smash into a comet.
The first public radio broadcast airs live opera from New York.
The Huygens probe lands on Titan, Saturn's largest moon.
Wikipedia goes online.
Shackleton's men reach what they believe is the South Magnetic Pole.
Captain Cook's ships become the first to cross the Antarctic Circle.
The Paris Peace Conference opens after the First World War.
New Horizons launches on its journey to Pluto.
Barack Obama is inaugurated as US president.
Concorde begins commercial supersonic passenger flights.
Apple's "1984" ad airs during the Super Bowl.
The bathyscaphe Trieste reaches the bottom of the Challenger Deep.
Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, sparking the California Gold Rush.
The first Winter Olympics open in Chamonix, France.
The First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove.
Thomas Edison is granted a patent for his incandescent lamp.
Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is published.
Karl Benz patents his petrol-powered motor car.
The Beatles play their final public concert on a London rooftop.
Explorer 1, the first US satellite, launches.
